ScrapedExchangeRate.description:
One exchange rate an institution applies, as a scraper read it.

Scoped to one product (`product`) or to the whole institution (None). The
writer only ever attaches it to an institution and product that already
exist: it never creates one to hang a rate on.

base_currency.description: Upper-case code of the currency being priced, e.g. 'USD'.
base_currency.title: Base Currency

product.description: The product of this institution the rate applies to; None for an institution-wide rate.

quote_currency.description: Upper-case code of the currency the rate is quoted in.
quote_currency.title: Quote Currency

rate.description: Quote units per 1 base unit (e.g. CLP per USD); positive, at most 8 decimals (stored as NUMERIC(20, 8)).
rate.title: Rate

reported_as_of.description: Validity date the institution prints next to the rate, if any.
reported_as_of.title: Reported As Of

source.description: Spanish label of where the rate was read, shown in the UI.
source.title: Source

ScrapedExchangeRate.title: ScrapedExchangeRate

ScrapedPriceHistory.description:
Daily closing prices of one product's unit (e.g. a stock), as read.

`product` names the product exactly as the scraper emits it. The writer
keeps one price per product and day, updates a day whose price changed,
and only ever attaches a series to a product that already exists: it
never creates one to hang prices on.

points.description: One closing price per trading day, each day at most once.
points.title: Points

product.description: The product of this institution whose unit the prices are for.

ScrapedPriceHistory.title: ScrapedPriceHistory

external_ref.title: External Ref

kind.description: Product kind; selects the attributes/metrics payload family.
kind.title: Kind

metrics.description: Per-scrape observation payload; snapshotted by the writer.

ScrapedTransaction.description: A transaction extracted by a scraper.

accounting_date.description: Date the institution posted the transaction, when it reports one separately from the date it occurred. Nullable: most sources report a single date, and a NULL simply means 'not reported'. Never part of a dedup key.
accounting_date.title: Accounting Date

amount.description: Signed amount in the transaction's currency: negative=expense, positive=income. At most 2 decimals (stored as NUMERIC(18, 2)); CLP amounts are whole numbers and may be sent as integers.
amount.title: Amount

internal_transfer.description: True when the movement only moves the user's money between their own products (e.g. a stock purchase paid from a cash wallet), so it is neither spending nor income. Stored as is_internal_transfer when the row is first written, and never rewritten by a re-scrape, so a user's change wins.
internal_transfer.title: Internal Transfer

location.description: Where the transaction happened, when the source reports it. Written only into location columns that are still NULL, and never onto a row whose location the user edited.

product_external_ref.description: external_ref of the product of this institution, product_kind and currency the transaction belongs to, for kinds with one product per holding (e.g. a stock position). Such a product is never created for a transaction: until a product leg has stored it, the transaction is left for a later run. None files it on the product with no external_ref, created if missing.
product_external_ref.title: Product External Ref

product_kind.description: Kind of the product the transaction belongs to, e.g. 'checking'.
product_kind.title: Product Kind

scheduled_month.description: First-of-month date the charge lands, for deferred/installment purchases.
scheduled_month.title: Scheduled Month

TransactionLocation.description:
Where a transaction happened, as far as its source says.

Every field is optional and independent of the others: a source that
reports only a city sends only `city`. Text is trimmed, blank means
absent, and nothing is re-cased (descriptions are stored as given too).
Coordinates come in pairs. Frozen, so it can ride on hashable records
such as a scraper's frozen dataclasses.

city.description: City, as the source spells it.
city.title: City

country.description: Country name as the source spells it (e.g. 'Chile'); a source that only reports an ISO 3166 code sends the code.
country.title: Country

name.description: Merchant or place name, when it differs from the description.
name.title: Name
